dropped: the hypothesis that the operands f,g are disk grid arrays (the page uses it implicitly when it calls the forward outputs 'all disk arrays')
the hypotheses of Lemma synthetic-transform-cost: t_i in {2^{l-1},2^l} (powers of two dividing 2r), r=2^l with 2<=l<p, dl<=C_l p, K=floor(d^c)<=l-1, p>=p_1
items.note: The page assembles the procedure, the normalization identity, the permutation-commuting argument, the cost total and the error chain exactly as in the proof of Proposition prop:synthetic-convolution. It leaves out the operand and transform-lemma hypotheses and the proposition's closing clause (the output is a disk array when one operand has norm <= rho and the bound is <= 1-rho). That clause is not part of the step as assigned.
It is a definition, given in full: 'For arrays over R_r define M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/(rM)=(f*g)/T', with M=prod t_i and T=rM defined just before.

dropped: each of the M first cyclic addresses determines one second address
each of the r first polynomial indices determines one second index modulo r
the negacyclic wrap supplies the sign
items.note: The page asserts 'A fixed output coefficient averages rM signed scalar products' with a citation and goes straight to the contraction bound. It does not give the counting that shows why there are exactly rM signed terms.

All parts of the procedure are on the page and are justified by the normalization argument. 'Perform both forward transforms and retain their common LB order', record products by Signed packing truncated by Q_p, the opposite transform applied 'without reordering', and 'scaling it by M'.

The page writes F^- with characters chi_j(k)=prod omega_{t_i}^{-j_i k_i}, uses chi_j(k+l)=chi_j(k)chi_j(l) and commutativity, and expands the double sum to get M(F^-f)(j)(F^-g)(j). This is the paper's 'expansion of the finite sums', carried out correctly.
The page obtains F^+F^-=I/M by tensoring the per-axis F_t^+F_t^-=I/t. Applying F^+ gives (f*g)/M=MF^+((F^-f)(F^-g)), and dividing by r gives the identity. This is correct and matches the paper.
'Since P acts on each record separately, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v). Because T_+LB=F^+, applying T_+ ... equals F^+P(F^-f,F^-g)'. This follows the paper, with the step T_+LB=F^+ made explicit.

It is a definition, given with the paper's values. 'delta=sqrt2 l 2^{-p} for the error of each transform procedure and eta=sqrt2 2^{-p} for one truncation Q_p', tied to the transform lemma's error bound.

The page splits P(u~,v~)-P(u,v)=P(u~-u,v~)+P(u,v~-v) and bounds each term by delta using ||P(x,y)||<=||x|| ||y|| and the disk bounds on v~ and u. This is the paper's argument. The bound on P is itself justified on the page: 'Each coefficient of uv is a signed sum of r products'.

It defines z~=Q_p(P(u~,v~)) and z_*=P(u,v) and adds the truncation error eta to 2delta. Elsewhere the page notes that Q_p 'keeps it in the disk', which is what lets the opposite procedure's bound apply to z~.

The page uses ||h~-T_+z~||<delta and the contractivity of T_+, which it justifies ('F^+ averages signed shifts and B^{-1}L^{-1} only permutes records'), with the triangle inequality to get <3delta+eta. This matches the paper.
'The exact multiplication by M gives total error less than M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}'. The arithmetic follows directly from the defined delta and eta.

The page charges O(rp log(rp)) per record product over M=T/r records, O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]) for each of the three transforms, and linear time for the final scaling, then sums them to the stated bound.

errors.quote: Put $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$, a power of $y$ that plays a $t$-th root of unity
errors.problem: omega_t=y^{2r/t} is defined only when t is a power of two dividing 2r. The page never restricts the axis lengths t_i, which it introduces only as 'the length of axis i'. The paper defines omega_t only for such t and takes t_i in {2^{l-1},2^l} under the hypotheses of Lemma synthetic-transform-cost.
